findings.description: NudgeRatchet is the only donor with neither a donation-disable switch nor a try/catch AND the only one without rescueERC20. The absent rescue hatch is justified in NatSpec by a 'self-cleaning' property (stray USDC is forwarded on the next dispatch) that story-046 made conditional on the state of a contract in another repository. While the streamer path is broken, every mint through this dispatcher index reverts and any USDC resident on the ratchet is unreachable by any actor.
findings.attackVector: Not attacker-driven. Triggers: (a) nudgeStreamer unset (post-deploy default, re-armed by NFTMinterV2.replaceDispatcher); (b) NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered after setBatchMinter to an unregistered sink; (c) NEW third-party trigger - a USDC blacklist on the streamer itself, a failure point that did not exist when the donation was a leaf safeTransfer, and which bricks every donor sharing that streamer at once. Recovery spans three contracts and up to three owner keys.
preconditions: dispatcher holds a non-zero USDC balance
any one of the trigger conditions
findings.impact: Mint availability halted at the dispatcher index; USDC on the dispatcher permanently unreachable while the condition persists.
findings.footgunBasis: Three of four structurally-similar donors degrade gracefully; the fourth halts minting. The NatSpec pre-declares the wedge accepted, but does not address the second-order consequence that the rescue hatch was omitted on a now-invalid rationale.

findings.description: If a whitelisted nudge token later becomes the derived payment token (owner repoints setDispatcherIndex/tokenMinter), _snapshotRewards skips it so it is never paid as a nudge, while the donors keep feeding collectNudge for the still-registered pair. The accumulated pot then becomes indistinguishable from payment-token residue and step 10 sweeps the FULL balance to msg.sender.
findings.attackVector: Permissionless first-come race: any caller invokes batchMint with count=1 and a trivial payment and receives the entire accumulated nudge pot as a 'dust refund'. The sweep is NOT gated on `qualifies`, so the nudgeSize earn-your-nudge gate is bypassed entirely, and the pot goes to msg.sender rather than recipient. Repeatable each time the pot refills.
preconditions: token X on the batchMinter nudge whitelist (mandatory for registerStream)
owner repoints dispatcherIndex/tokenMinter so X becomes the derived payment token
highly reachable: NudgeRatchet, Uniboost and PromotionUniV2_Eth are all USDC-prime dispatchers, so pinning the batchMinter to any of them makes USDC the payment token
findings.impact: Entire accumulated nudge pot captured by an arbitrary caller, bypassing the nudgeSize gate.
findings.rootCauseNote: Root-cause lines are in phoenix-nft-staking (a nested lib/ dependency of this repo). Filed as an integration hazard because the reachability is created by this repo's USDC-prime dispatcher set. Not created by stories 046/047, but the change enlarges the quiet-accumulation window and moves value through a streamer that has no owner rescue of its own.

findings.description: Stories 046/047 route four donors through the NudgeStreamer to prevent a batchMint caller capturing a donation burst. NudgeRatchetDelayRelease - the one donor whose entire design is to emit discrete admin-timed lumps - was left on a direct safeTransfer to the batchMinter, bypassing the streamer's metering entirely.
findings.attackVector: release() is onlyReleaser and therefore an identifiable public mempool transaction. Because batchMint snapshots the pot pre-loop, a searcher back-runs release() with a qualifying batchMint in the same block and captures the entire released lump - exactly the burst-capture the streamer exists to prevent.
preconditions: DelayRelease and the streamed donors share a batchMinter (implied by the identical batchMinter field and 6-dp USDC guard)
findings.impact: Whole released lump captured by one back-running batcher instead of streaming to honest batchers over the window.

findings.description: story-047 replaced `require(gemAmt > 0, "donation dust")` with `if (gemAmt > 0)`. The require used to revert into the caller's catch and emit DonationSkipped; the if returns silently emitting nothing. The contract NatSpec still tells operators to monitor DonationSkipped. Simultaneously the caught region widened from PSM-only to PSM + streamer wiring + the streamer's outbound settle transfer, so DonationSkipped became the sole signal for a strictly larger failure set at the moment it stopped covering one of them.
findings.attackVector: Not attacker-driven. A streamer misconfiguration (unset, NotRegistered, blacklisted settle target, PSM gem drift) runs indefinitely with the nudge incentive dead while hook.onDispatch keeps accruing mint-debt on the gross amount.
preconditions: gemAmt floors to zero (dust sweep) OR any newly-swallowed streamer revert
findings.impact: Observability only. _psmDonate is atomic so nothing is stranded mid-route, and phUSD backing is unimpaired (the un-donated USDS remains protocol-held on the pooler). What dies silently is the batch-minter reward incentive.

findings.description: (a) The sweep-and-retry that recovers parked USDS lives inside `if (donationEnabled)`. Disabling the donation while USDS is parked takes that USDS out of the retry loop; it is never re-swept and never wrapped to sUSDS, so it stops contributing to pool(). Recoverable only via rescueERC20, which the NatSpec does not present as the fallback. (b) `gem` is read live from ISkyPSM(psm).gem() every call, so a setPSM repoint to a different-gem PSM silently yields an unregistered (batchMinter, newGem) pair -> caught -> USDS parks with only a DonationSkipped event.
findings.attackVector: Not attacker-driven; owner-configuration footgun with a non-obvious consequence.
preconditions: USDS parked from a prior skipped donation
owner disables the donation OR repoints setPSM to a different-gem PSM
findings.impact: Idle, non-productive collateral on the pooler; fully recoverable but silent. No unbacked phUSD.

findings.type: widened trust surface on an unvalidated token
findings.description: Uniboost takes primeToken_ as a free constructor argument with no decimals/standard guard, unlike NudgeRatchet and NudgeRatchetDelayRelease which both require decimals() == 6. Post-story-046 the donation branch has no try/catch, so a live donation makes mint success depend on TWO token movements inside a foreign contract (safeTransferFrom donor->streamer and safeTransfer streamer->recipient) instead of one leaf transfer.
findings.attackVector: A blacklisting prime token that blocks either the streamer or the recipient bricks every mint through this dispatcher. Fee-on-transfer would make collectNudge's `buffer += amount` overstate the held balance for that pair (shortfall lands on the last claimant of that pair; _accrued's buffer cap preserves other pairs' solvency) - noted only for completeness, FoT is a C4 known-invalid class.
preconditions: Uniboost deployed with a non-plain prime token
findings.impact: Mint availability at this dispatcher index; the missing deploy-time guard is the in-scope defect.

findings.type: unbounded input to a slippage-floored swap
findings.description: _legB swaps address(this).balance in full rather than the ETH produced by the preceding swapExactTokensForETH. receive() is open to anyone and rescueETH's own NatSpec acknowledges a failed/partial Leg B can leave resident ETH. minPromoOut is calibrated by the pooler for the expected 30%-leg ETH only, so resident or donated ETH inflates the swapped amount without inflating the floor.
findings.attackVector: A griefer front-sends ETH to inflate the swap beyond the priced floor and sandwiches it (cost-bearing, they fund the excess). More realistically, a stale residual from a prior partial pool reaches the same miscalibrated state with no attacker at all.
preconditions: non-zero resident ETH at pool() time
findings.impact: The slippage floor stops bounding Leg B's swap; larger-than-priced sandwich exposure.
findings.carryover: run-17 L-13 (whole-balance ETH sweep + receive() footgun) - CONFIRMED still live after the story-045 six-arg pool() rework
findings.scopeNote: PromotionUniV2_Eth was absent from the cached scope array; this run gave it a full first-pass read.

findings.description: phusdBurned = phusdAcquired / 2 uses Leg A's return value, but _addPhusdPromoLiquidity pools IERC20(phUSD).balanceOf(address(this)) and IERC20(promotionToken).balanceOf(address(this)). Residual phUSD from a prior pool()'s router refund, or a third-party donation, is pooled without a matching burn, so the documented 'half burned, halves value-matched' property holds only when the contract starts each pool() at a zero phUSD balance.
findings.attackVector: Not attacker-driven; minLP bounds the outcome.
preconditions: non-zero resident phUSD or promotion token at pool() time
findings.impact: Documentation-fidelity / accounting drift in the 30/30 value match. No value leak identified.

refuted.hypothesis: Lead 4 - residual streamer allowance is exploitable
refuted.basis: All four donors forceApprove the exact amount and collectNudge pulls exactly that amount (NudgeStreamer.sol:149) in the same call, so the standing allowance is zero on success and rolled back on any failure. A residual requires an under-pulling collectNudge, i.e. an owner repointing nudgeStreamer at a hostile contract - an obvious owner action, suppressed under Law 3. The asymmetry with the adjacent forceApprove(psm, 0) is style, not a vector.

refuted.hypothesis: Lead 5 - batchMinter's own nudgeStreamer unset means donations accumulate in the streamer and never flush into the pot
refuted.basis: collectNudge calls _settle on every donor deposit (NudgeStreamer.sol:146), which transfers the accrued amount to the batchMinter whether or not the batchMinter knows about the streamer. With BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.nudgeStreamer == 0 the step-3.5 flush is skipped, but funds still arrive - they land after the current batch's pre-loop snapshot rather than before it. Net effect is a one-batch delay. A true strand needs donor dispatches to cease entirely AND the pointer to stay zero, and is cured by one setNudgeStreamer call. Recorded as an ops note.

refuted.hypothesis: Lead 3 - widened catch lets mint-debt accrue against value that never arrives (unbacked phUSD)
refuted.basis: hook.onDispatch fires on the gross amount regardless, but the un-donated USDS stays on the pooler, so phUSD backing is not impaired - the protocol still holds the asset, as raw USDS rather than sUSDS or a nudge payout. The real gap is incentive availability, folded into CODE-004/CODE-005. No unbacked-phUSD path found.

driftWatches.basis: No new conversion on any donation path; the amount handed to collectNudge is byte-identical to the amount computed one line earlier in all four (NudgeRatchet:160 bal, Uniboost:250 and PromotionUniV2_Eth:396 donationAmount, BalancerPoolerV2:347 gemAmt). NudgeStreamer.PRECISION=1e18 cancels between rate and accrual, so buffers and transfers stay in native units.
NudgeRatchet:137-140 and NudgeRatchetDelayRelease retain the hookTypeId() guard; ATokenDispatcherV2.setHook:95 still rejects zero and hook is never null. Stories 046/047 touched no hook wiring.
No new hook-scaled arithmetic in this range.

reentrancyChecklist.basis: No donor writes local state after collectNudge; only an emit follows. dispatch is nonReentrant (ATokenDispatcherV2:120).
OZ ReentrancyGuard is contract-wide, so pool() on all three poolers is locked for the duration of dispatch. _psmDonate is external but self-gated (BalancerPoolerV2:310).
Same contract-wide guard; getIdealBPT/primeToken/withdrawBPT/rescueERC20 mutate no shared accounting.

No donor exposes a price/share view consumed as an oracle. More decisively there is no inbound callback window in the donation path at all: USDC/USDS have no transfer hooks, so neither _settle's outbound transfer nor collectNudge's pull yields control. The clearance rests on the token being hook-free - see CODE-006 for Uniboost, the one donor whose token is unpinned.

NFTMinterV2._executeMint:196 invokes onERC1155Received on an attacker-controlled recipient after dispatch, and inside batchMint that happens while paymentToken.forceApprove(nftMinter, type(uint256).max) is live (BatchNFTMinterMultiToken:459). Not exploitable: _executeMint:183 always pulls via safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, ...), so a re-entering attacker spends their own funds, and mintFor is authorizedMinters-gated. batchMint is nonReentrant. The hook can reach the permissionless collectNudge, but the batcher's payout was snapshotted pre-loop, so a mid-loop donation cannot be recovered in the same batch.
Neither donor nor recipient nor streamer registers an ERC-1820 interface, so the hooks would not fire even with an ERC777 prime token.
